text: Millions of people are watching GTA 6 right now, and most of that giant city isn't even there.
Big open world games are way too huge to fit in a console's memory all at once.
So they only load the chunk of the world around you, and keep swapping new pieces in as you move.
And anything outside the camera's view gets skipped. The game just stops drawing it.
Turn around, and it gets drawn again so fast you would never notice.
Stuff far away is a cheap, blocky copy. As you get closer, the game swaps in a better one.
Even buildings hidden behind other buildings get skipped, since they're blocked from view anyway.
And the game redoes all of this up to sixty times every single second.
If the game falls behind, things pop out of nowhere. Gamers call that pop in.
So the city only really exists right where you're looking. Everything else is just waiting to be built.
Follow for more of the secret tricks behind your favorite games.
